plain_english: In this being, being arises corrupted, by division-nature — flaw of being; like a couch, in this suffering-stream surely flows — what raft by that?
sanskrit_cite: asmin sati bhavati bhavo duṣṭo bhedātmaneti bhavadoṣaḥ mañcavadasmin duḥkhasroto@ṇūn vahati yatplavastena

plain_english: The rest are easily-accessible forms; words there infer meaning appropriately — cause of samsara is action, sprout of samsara is called.
sanskrit_cite: śeṣāstu sugamarūpāḥ śabdāstatrārthamūhayeducitam saṃsārakāraṇaṃ karma saṃsārāṅkura ucyate

plain_english: Fourteenfold being-diversity is action-born, because — therefore indeed in Samkhya Yoga Pancaratra and teachings.
sanskrit_cite: caturdaśavidhaṃ bhūtavaiciatryaṃ karmajaṃ yataḥ ata eva sāṃkhyayogapāñcarātrādiśāsane

plain_english: 'I-mine' thus complete abandonment is taught for actionlessness — actionless indeed, when established in root-impurity even in ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃmameti saṃtyāgo naiṣkarmyāyopadiśyate niṣkarmā hi sthite mūlamale@pyajñānanāmani

plain_english: From variety-cause-absence, neither upward moves nor even downward — only by limitation, not touching Shiva-nondifference.
sanskrit_cite: vaicitryakāraṇābhāvānnordhva sarati nāpyadhaḥ kevalaṃ pārimityena śivābhedamasaṃspṛśan

plain_english: Consciousness-alone is called, established in pure-consciousness-alone — he again from Shambhava-will, contemplating Shiva-nondifference.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānakevalī proktaḥ śuddhacinmātrasaṃsthitaḥ sa punaḥ śāṃbhavecchātaḥ śivābhedaṃ parāmṛśan

plain_english: Gradually mantra-lord-that-guide-formed, he goes to Shiva-selfhood — indeed whose is this cause? If karma-impurity, how?
sanskrit_cite: kramānmantreśatannetṛrūpo yāti śivātmatām nanu kāraṇametasya karmaṇaścenmalaḥ katham

plain_english: He even of vijnanakala does not produce karma-continuity — not so; he indeed, impurity in jnanakala would destroy — how?
sanskrit_cite: sa vijñānākalasyāpi na sūte karmasaṃtatim maivaṃ sa hi malo jñānākale didhvaṃsiṣuḥ katham

plain_english: Cause would be destruction-sameness, from freedom alone would arise — in the called destroying-destroyed-destroyed, in three, then.
sanskrit_cite: hetuḥ syāddhvaṃsamānatvaṃ svātantryādeva codbhavet didhvaṃsiṣudhvaṃsamānadhvastākhyāsu tisṛṣvatha

plain_english: Within ten states, in created state-intervals, from own-sequence abiding — vijnana-akala-mantresa-tadisa-etc. conception.
sanskrit_cite: daśāsvantaḥ kṛtāvasthāntarāsu svakramasthiteḥ vijñānākalamantreśatadīśāditvakalpanā

plain_english: In the fourth state, called sleep, manifold difference will be explained; therefore own power becomes totally oriented toward destruction.
sanskrit_cite: tataśca supte turye ca vakṣyate bahubhedatā ataḥ pradhvaṃsanaunmukhyakhilībhūtasvaśaktikaḥ

plain_english: Let impurity not be called the cause of action; action is not from impurity, since action is activity-natured.
sanskrit_cite: karmaṇo hetutāmetu malaḥ kathamivocyatām kiṃ ca karmāpi na malādyataḥ karma kriyātmakam

plain_english: Activity comes from the form of agency and freedom, not again from impurity; action-hood is the varied fruit-giving of this action.
sanskrit_cite: kriyā ca kartṛtārūpāt svātantryānna punarmalāt yā tvasya karmaṇaścitraphaladatvena karmatā

plain_english: That well-known action-hood is not without contraction in the self; impurity regards varied different fruit as enjoyable.
sanskrit_cite: prasiddhā sā na saṃkocaṃ vinātmani malaśca saḥ vicitraṃ hi phalaṃ bhinnaṃ bhogyatvenābhimanyate

plain_english: In the enjoyer-self, this difference-form arrangement exists; thus it resorts to cooperation in the production of its own work.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktaryātmani teneyaṃ bhedarūpā vyavasthitiḥ iti svakāryaprasave sahakāritvamāśrayan

plain_english: Impurity is the cause as power-manifesting of action; but if action exists, how can impurity also exist?
sanskrit_cite: sāmarthyavyañjakatvena karmaṇaḥ kāraṇaṃ malaḥ nanvevaṃ karmasadbhāvānmalasyāpi sthiteḥ katham

plain_english: Limited knowledge has contraction; such contraction indeed exists; even destroyed contraction becomes firm by meditation.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānākalatā tasya saṃkoco hyasti tādṛśaḥ maivamadhvastasaṃkoco@pyasau bhāvanayā dṛḍham

plain_english: Thinking 'I am not the doer,' one abandons action impression; the firm disposition in the self says this action will fruit.
sanskrit_cite: nāhaṃ karteti manvānaḥ karmasaṃskāramujjhati phaliṣyatīdaṃ karmeti yā dṛḍhā vṛttirātmani

plain_english: That impression is for fruit here, not for causing remembering; even in undestroyed contraction, meditation on 'I am not the doer' acts.
sanskrit_cite: sa saṃskāraḥ phalāyeha na tu smaraṇakāraṇam apradhvaste@pi saṃkoce nāhaṃ karteti bhāvanāt

plain_english: Fruit does not arise for the intoxicated or deluded, nor when penance is done; austerity performed by me today would clearly be for him.
sanskrit_cite: na phalaṃ kṣīvamūḍhādeḥ prāyaścitte@tha vā kṛte yanmayādya tapastaptaṃ tadasmai syāditi sphuṭam

plain_english: Action of an intentional agent does not fruit from intention; but intention-named action in the mental sphere is impression.
sanskrit_cite: abhisaṃdhimataḥ karma na phaledabhisandhitaḥ tathābhisaṃdhānākhyāṃ tu mānase karma saṃskriyām

plain_english: Producing fruit-stained action becomes fit for fruit attainment; whoever even there with firmness abandons fruit impression.
sanskrit_cite: phaloparaktāṃ vidadhatkalpate phalasampade yastu tatrāpi dārḍhyena phalasaṃskāramujjhati

plain_english: He enjoys a special fruit made by abandoning that fruit; by this method one abandons all action-continuity.
sanskrit_cite: sa tatphalatyāgakṛtaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ phalamaśnute anayā paripāṭyā yaḥ samastāṃ karmasaṃtatim

plain_english: With non-ego union one should abandon; even the limited one with contraction should do so; but some wrong action is own and intentional.
sanskrit_cite: anahaṃyutayā projjhet sasaṃkoco@pi so@kalaḥ nanvitthaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcidātmīyamabhisaṃdhitaḥ

plain_english: Real speech would not be known to another by you; if the enjoyer's intention were as in oneself, it would differ.
sanskrit_cite: parasmai syānna vijñātaṃ bhavatā tāttvikaṃ vacaḥ tasya bhoktustathā cetsyādabhisaṃdhiryathātmani

plain_english: That wrong action would necessarily be of another too; in knowing another's intention, one's own intention becomes firm.
sanskrit_cite: tadavaśyaṃ parasyāpi satastadduṣkṛtaṃ bhavet parābhisaṃdhisaṃvittau svābhisaṃdhirdṛḍhībhavet

plain_english: In absence of intention there is no fruit-connection; the convention 'wrong action is mine' is for fruitlessness.
sanskrit_cite: abhisaṃdhānavirahe tvasya no phalayogitā na me duṣkṛtamityeṣā rūḍhistasyāphalāya sā

plain_english: In cutting another's intention, not intended by self, fruit would not be for both due to destruction-cause arrangement.
sanskrit_cite: parābhisandhivicchede svātmanānabhisaṃhitau dvayorapi phalaṃ na syānnāśahetuvyavasthiteḥ

plain_english: In pleasure-cause and pleasure of this, from common intention even from undifferentiated, just enjoyment of virtue-etc fruit.
sanskrit_cite: sukhahetau sukhe cāsya sāmānyādabhisaṃdhitaḥ nirviśeṣādapi nyāyyā dharmādiphalabhoktṛtā

plain_english: Suffering or suffering-cause would be thus mine; but common intention would not be of that unrighteousness, nor scripture.
sanskrit_cite: duḥkhaṃ me duḥkhaheturvā stādityeṣa punarna tu sāmānyo@pyabhisaṃdhiḥ syāttadadharmasya nāgamaḥ

plain_english: We speak the topic of the described limited knower: with non-ego union all action impressions are dissolved.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtaṃ brūmahe jñānākalasyoktacarasya yat anahaṃyutayā sarvā vilīnāḥ karmasaṃskriyāḥ

plain_english: Therefore for this one action does not exist; impurity may do cooperation for anyone, and by that this one attains destruction-nature.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādasya na karmāsti kasyāpi sahakāritām malaḥ karotu tenāyaṃ dhvaṃsamānatvamaśnute

plain_english: With destroyed impurity, controlled by inner Shiva possession, even ego-state goes, not action-dependent condition.
sanskrit_cite: apadhvastamalastvantaḥśivāveśavaśīkṛtaḥ ahaṃbhāvaparo@pyeti na karmādhīnavṛttitām

plain_english: Said in holy previous scripture by the supreme lord: they desire impurity as ignorance, cause of the world sprout.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca tadetatparameśinā malamajñānamicchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam

plain_english: Merit-demerit-natured action, pleasure-pain-etc.-marked — mark pleasure-pain and the rest as own effect, from cause-state.
sanskrit_cite: dharmādharmātmakaṃ karma sukhaduḥkhādilakṣaṇam lakṣayetsukhaduḥkhādi svaṃ kārya hetubhāvataḥ

plain_english: No cause ever exists without its own effect — causality is just that fitness, conditioned by fruit-immediacy.
sanskrit_cite: nahi hetuḥ kadāpyāste vinā kārya nijaṃ kvacit hetutā yogyataivāsau phalānantaryabhāvitā

plain_english: But prior causality through succession — and what is that — is observed through pleasure-pain in common, where the cause is seen.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvakasya tu hetutvaṃ pāramparyeṇa kiṃ ca tat lakṣyate sukhaduḥkhādyaiḥ samāne dṛṣṭakāraṇe

plain_english: Through various causes, something else here from seeing action — in own limb grace-roughness and the rest arising by own action.
sanskrit_cite: citrairhetvantaraṃ kiṃcittacca karmeha darśanāt svāṅge prasādaraukṣyādi jāyamānaṃ svakarmaṇā

plain_english: Seen situated in another body, action as cause is inferred — here too in other bodies situated, clearly in action-fruit, because.
sanskrit_cite: dṛṣṭamityanyadehasthaṃ kāraṇaṃ karma kalpyāte ihāpyanyānyadehasthe sphuṭaṃ karmaphale yataḥ

plain_english: Farming-action in spring, enjoyment in autumn, and another body — of the single investigator, origin however whence-thence.
sanskrit_cite: kṛṣikarma madhau bhogaḥ śaradyanyā ca sā tanuḥ anusaṃdhāturekasya saṃbhavastu yatastataḥ

plain_english: Of that very one wonderful is its fruit whose action is ancient — even drunk, if the king commands the cook in the morning, such: feed.
sanskrit_cite: tasyaiva tatphalaṃ citraṃ karma yasya purātanam kṣīvo@pi rājā sūdaṃ cedādiśetprātarīdṛśam

plain_english: Without feeding-intention he obtains that fruit — thus other-birth-acquired action even by present intention-holding.
sanskrit_cite: bhojayetyanusaṃdhānādvinā prāpnoti tatphalam itthaṃ janmāntaropāttakarmāpyadyānusaṃdhinā

plain_english: Without, he enjoys fruit — the cause there is the eastern unshaken; therefore action done, by action or even by austerity.
sanskrit_cite: vinā bhuṅkte phalaṃ hetustatra prācyā hyakampatā ata eva kṛtaṃ karma karmaṇā tapasāpi vā

plain_english: By knowledge it would be stopped, toward fruit-ripening — begun action in this body; but what of further action — how then?
sanskrit_cite: jñānena vā nirudhyeta phalapākeṣvanunmukham ārabdhakāryaṃ dehe@smin yatpunaḥ karma tatkatham

plain_english: Let the last ten be cut — to restrain is indeed impossible; there in the body, what other, today-born or ancient.
sanskrit_cite: ucchidyatāmantyadaśaṃ niroddhuṃ nahi śakyate tatraiva dehe yattvanyadadyagaṃ vā purātanam

plain_english: Action by that knowledge-initiation and the rest is overpowered into eunuch-hood — thus conditioning-firmness indeed, for fruit firmness again.
sanskrit_cite: karma tajjñānadīkṣādyaiḥ śaṇḍhīkartuṃ prasahyate tathā saṃskāradārḍhya hi phalāya dṛḍhatā punaḥ

plain_english: When karma is destroyed, then even unmade action remains under delusion's dependence.
sanskrit_cite: yadā yadā vinaśyeta karmadhvastaṃ tadā tadā ato mohaparādhīno yadyapyakṛta kiṃcana

plain_english: Even so, at knowledge-time all of that is burned, as the lord, giver and taker, all-seeing, has said.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi jñānakāle tatsarvameva pradahyate uktaṃ ca śrīpare@hānādānaḥ sarvadṛgulvaṇaḥ

plain_english: In a moment all is burned: body-residing unmade and made action, through taking identity with the body.
sanskrit_cite: muhūrtānnirdahetsarva dehasthamakṛtaṃ kṛtam dehasthamiti dehena saha tādātmyamāśritā

plain_english: By free will consciousness, there-standing karma is burned through abandoning body-unity desire and resting in world-self state.
sanskrit_cite: svācchandyātsaṃvidevoktā tatrasthaṃ karma dahyate dehaikyavāsanātyāgāt sa ca viśvātmatāsthiteḥ

plain_english: In untimely ripening, the pervading undivided impression is indeed contraction, and he too is body-unity-made.
sanskrit_cite: akālakalite vyāpinyabhinne yā hi saṃskriyā saṃkoca eva sānena so@pi dehaikatāmayaḥ

plain_english: This karma impurity is said to be such that dissolution powers lie within the cave-depth like sleeping creepers.
sanskrit_cite: etatkārmamalaṃ proktaṃ yena sākaṃ layākalāḥ syurguhāgahanāntaḥsthāḥ suptā iva sarīsṛpāḥ

plain_english: Then awakened impressions, as fitting share holders, flow again and again from brahma to the immovable end.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ prabuddhasaṃskārāste yathocitabhāginaḥ brahmādisthāvarānte@smin saṃsranti punaḥ punaḥ

plain_english: Those again, for loss of karma impressions, with begun meditations, not reaching meditation completion, go to dissolution.
sanskrit_cite: ye punaḥ karmasaṃskārahānyai prārabdhabhāvanāḥ bhāvanāpariniṣpattimaprāpya pralayaṃ gatāḥ

plain_english: They attain great mantra-hood through excellence of inner meditation ripeness, and varied results from karma.
sanskrit_cite: mahāntaṃ te tathāntaḥsthabhāvanāpākasauṣṭhavāt mantratvaṃ pratipadyante citrāccitraṃ ca karmataḥ

plain_english: Of this karma impurity going along the maya-end path, the chief cause is said to be the ignorance-atom impurity.
sanskrit_cite: asya kārmamalasyeyanmāyāntādhvavisāriṇaḥ pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ proktamajñānātmāṇavo malaḥ

plain_english: The agitation of this lolika-named thing clearly stands through cooperation and standing fitness depending on the lord's will.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobho@sya lolikākhyasya sahakāritayā sphuṭam tiṣṭhāsāyogyataunmukhyamīśvarecchāvaśācca tat

plain_english: Without consciousness, inert support is not capable anywhere, because atoms are named and the great lord alone is light-self.
sanskrit_cite: na jaḍaścidadhiṣṭhānaṃ vinā kvāpi kṣamo yataḥ aṇavo nāma naivānyatprakāśātmā maheśvaraḥ

plain_english: The individual shines as both consciousness and non-consciousness; as field-knower and animal he is pervasive, without qualities, and actionless.
sanskrit_cite: cidacidrūpatābhāsī pudgalaḥ kṣetravitpaśuḥ cidrūpatvācca sa vyāpī nirguṇo niṣkriyastataḥ

plain_english: The eternal, formless desirer of yoga is declared; ignorance comes from non-consciousness, and difference arises between enjoyer and enjoyed.
sanskrit_cite: yogopāyepsako nityo mūrtivandhyaḥ prabhāṣyate acittvādajñatā bhedo bhogyādbhoktrantarādatha

plain_english: That impurity of those atoms awakens strongly by the lord's will; thus it is said in the scripture named Sripurva.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāmaṇūnāṃ sa mala īśvarecchāvaśādbhṛśam prabudhyate tathā coktaṃ śāstre śrīpūrvanāmani

plain_english: By the lord's will, desire for enjoyment arises; the first mantra great lord helps that enjoyment desire.
sanskrit_cite: īśvarecchāvaśādasya bhogecchā saṃprajāyate bhogecchorupakārārthamādyo mantramaheśvaraḥ

plain_english: Having agitated maya, he creates variegated samsara; maya is named the god's non-separate power.
sanskrit_cite: māyāṃ vikṣobhya saṃsāraṃ nirmimīte vicitrakam māyā ca nāma devasya śaktiravyatirekiṇī

plain_english: Thus independence of difference-appearance: he is made by her as the first difference-appearance, which has not reached separation.
sanskrit_cite: bhedāvabhāsasvātantryaṃ tathāhi sa tayā kṛtaḥ ādyo bhedāvabhāso yo vibhāgamanupeyivān

plain_english: She is the appearance containing infinite beings; supreme night is inert because of difference-form, and her effect is inert for that reason.
sanskrit_cite: garbhīkṛtānantabhāvivibhāsā sā parā niśā sā jaḍā bhedarūpatvāt kāryaṃ cāsyā jaḍaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: Pervading because it causes the universe, subtle because of single effect-conception, and eternal one because of inseparability of shiva and power, it is the root cause.
sanskrit_cite: vyāpinī viśvahetutvāt sūkṣmā kāryaikakalpanāt śivaśaktyavinābhāvānnityaikā mūlakāraṇam

plain_english: All effect is unconscious and many-self, as a pot is primary; therefore effect is not self, but conscious.
sanskrit_cite: acetanamanekātma sarva kārya yathā ghaṭaḥ pradhānaṃ ca tathā tasmāt kārya nātmā tu cetanaḥ

plain_english: Therefore in the path it was declared before that maya is twofold; god's maya-power approaches as differentiating.
sanskrit_cite: ata evādhvani proktā pūrvaṃ māyā dvidhā sthitā yathā ca māyā devasya śaktirabhyeti bhedinam

plain_english: Thus another, kala and so on, expands reality-nature by restricted power, having limited agency.
sanskrit_cite: tattvabhāvaṃ tathānyo@pi kalādistattvavistaraḥ niruddhaśakteryā kiṃcitkartṛtodvalanātmikā

plain_english: The lord's power, throwing the man below, is called kala; thus vidya and others, ending in earth, are ultimately so.
sanskrit_cite: nāthasya śaktiḥ sādhastātpuṃsaḥ kṣeptrī kalocyate evaṃ vidyādayo@pyete dharāntāḥ paramārthataḥ

plain_english: Siva-Sakti-made indeed, per stated reasoning — yet that distinct appearance of kala and the rest is by Isvara-will.
sanskrit_cite: śivaśaktimayā eva proktanyāyānusārataḥ tathāpi yatpṛthagbhānaṃ kalāderīśvarecchayā

plain_english: Then in inertness, in effected-ness, in separate-tattva-state certainly — the material cause is remembered as Maya; sometimes that effect only.
sanskrit_cite: tato jaḍatve kāryatve pṛthaktattvasthitau dhruvam upādānaṃ smṛtā māyā kvacittatkāryameva ca

plain_english: Thus-appearing variegated, form mutually excluded — what shines in imagination exists, like pot, outside.
sanskrit_cite: tathāvabhāsacitraṃ ca rūpamanyonyavarjitam yadbhāti kila saṃkalpe tadasti ghaṭavadvahiḥ

plain_english: Sky-flower and the rest — existence we assert, therefore no invalidity; the sky-flower, time-direction-mother-dependent, by the word 'does not exist.'
sanskrit_cite: khapuṣpādyastitāṃ brūmastato na vyabhicāritā khapuṣpaṃ kāladiṅmātṛsāpekṣaṃ nāstiśabdataḥ

plain_english: Like earth and the rest, thus absolute absence too be distinguished — what is to be imagined, thus of that the outer body is conscious.
sanskrit_cite: dharādivat tathātyantābhāvo@pyevaṃ vivicyatām yatsaṃkalpyaṃ tathā tasya bahirdeho@sti cetanaḥ

plain_english: Ending with Caitra Vatsa Ausiva — all that, such-bodied — whose body as his, of that kind the city outside.
sanskrit_cite: caitravatsauśivāntaṃ tat sarva tādṛśadehavat yasya deho yathā tasya tajjātīyaṃ puraṃ bahiḥ

plain_english: Therefore up to Susiva the world-path is established — of selves, that city to be attained, like another place by being a place.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ suśivaparyantā siddhā bhuvanapaddhatiḥ ātmanām tatpuraṃ prāpyaṃ deśatvādanyadeśavat

plain_english: Self path-enjoyership then by effort is accomplished — that Maya, agitated, births the universe all around.
sanskrit_cite: ātmanāmadhvabhoktṛtvaṃ tato@yatnena siddhyati sā māyā kṣobhamāpannā viśvaṃ sūte samantataḥ

plain_english: Like amla struck by a stick, fruits indeed although — nevertheless thus, from variegated prior-posterior manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: daṇḍāhatevāmalakī phalāni kila yadyapi tathāpi tu tathā citrapaurvāparyāvabhāsanāt

plain_english: Even in Maya-effect, in the tattva-flood, cause-effect mutual — though in other scriptures clearly seen in many ways.
sanskrit_cite: māyākārye@pi tattvaughe kāryakāraṇatā mithaḥ sā yadyapyanyaśāstreṣu bahudhā dṛśyate sphuṭam

plain_english: Nevertheless by Malini-scripture view we declare — from kala to earth, which ends in Maya, they declare.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi mālinīśāstradṛśā tāṃ saṃpracakṣmahe kalādivasudhāntaṃ yanmāyāntaḥ saṃpracakṣate

plain_english: This is distinct for each self, by pleasure-pain distinction — in one world only, in the enjoyment-means aggregate.
sanskrit_cite: pratyātmabhinnamevaitat sukhaduḥkhādibhedataḥ ekasyāmeva jagati bhogasādhanasaṃhatau

plain_english: Of pleasures equal manifestation — whence would experience-difference be? Not by karma-difference either, from that very impossibility.
sanskrit_cite: sukhādīnāṃ samaṃ vyakterbhogabhedaḥ kuto bhavet na cāsau karmabhedena tasyaivānupapattitaḥ

plain_english: Therefore the kala-beginning class is ever indeed distinct — it attains unity by Lord-will in dance song and playing.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt kalādiko vargo bhinna eva kadācana aikyametīśvarecchāto nṛttagītādivādane

plain_english: Of these kala-beginning tattvas, of all future ones, purity belongs to those purified by power-descent.
sanskrit_cite: eṣāṃ kalāditattvānāṃ sarveṣāmapi bhāvinām śuddhatvamasti teṣāṃ ye śaktipātapavitritāḥ

plain_english: For kala indeed pure, such-like, produces karma-nature — limited even so, quickly, by which from this samsara one is freed.
sanskrit_cite: kalā hi śuddhā tattādṛk karmatvaṃ saṃprasūyate mitamapyāśu yenāsmāt saṃsārādeṣa mucyate

plain_english: Raga vidya kala yati prakrti aksa artha collection — thus pure, having proclaimed, the guru in honor-praise, the all-lord.
sanskrit_cite: rāgavidyākālayatiprakṛtyakṣārthasaṃcayaḥ itthaṃ śuddha iti procya gururmānastutau vibhuḥ

plain_english: Thus this origin of kala and the rest is distinguished — from Maya-principle kala arose, marked by limited doership.
sanskrit_cite: evameṣā kalādīnāmutpattiḥ pravivicyate māyātattvāt kalā jātā kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇā

plain_english: Maya indeed produces difference from consciousness-full, from Shiva, of the bound — imposes a deep-sleep-like state; from that only, perception-and-action-less.
sanskrit_cite: māyā hi cinmayādbhedaṃ śivādvidadhatī paśoḥ suṣuptatāmivādhatte tata eva hyadṛkkriyaḥ

plain_english: For kala produces limited doership from self-embrace of the atom — of that too, atom with atom mutually; in collyrium she is born.
sanskrit_cite: kalā hi kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ sūte svāliṅganādaṇoḥ tasyāścāpyaṇunānyonyaṃ hyañjane sā prasūyate

plain_english: In immediate-liberation-initiation-born male-separation indeed, she being — clinging too and not producing — still own fruit somewhere.
sanskrit_cite: sadyonirvāṇadīkṣotthapuṃviśleṣe hi sā satī śliṣyantyapi ca no sūte tathāpi svaphalaṃ kvacit

plain_english: Like swelling first and like subtle sprout — from seed-water-fire-earth-shell-husk union, the birth-maker.
sanskrit_cite: ucchūnateva prathamā sūkṣmāṅkurakaleva ca bījasyāmbvagnimṛtkambutuṣayogāt prasūtikṛt

plain_english: Kala, Maya-atom-union-born — the unchanging makes material cause not the atom, but mutable Maya.
sanskrit_cite: kalā māyāṇusaṃyogajāpyeṣā nirvikārakam nāṇuṃ kuryādupādānaṃ kiṃtu māyāṃ vikāriṇīm

plain_english: Impurity and covering, Maya the becoming's material cause — action may be co-cause indeed toward pleasure-pain origin.
sanskrit_cite: malaścāvārako māyā bhāvopādānakāraṇam karma syāt sahakāryeva sukhaduḥkhodbhavaṃ prati

plain_english: Therefore concealed-consciousness-uplifting-action-doing, of Ananta-lord power only — by power impelled, inert.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ saṃcchannacaitanyasamudbalanakāryakṛt kalaivānantanāthasya śaktyā saṃpreritā jaḍā

plain_english: Not even the Lord's power will strengthen his consciousness — that strengthened, that indeed would not reach any doership.
sanskrit_cite: na ceśaśaktirevāsya caitanyaṃ balayiṣyati tadupodbalitaṃ taddhi na kiṃcitkartṛtāṃ vrajet

plain_english: This kala is no principal instrument, as knowledge and the rest — in man as agent she is agent, by being instigator, because.
sanskrit_cite: seyaṃ kalā na karaṇaṃ mukhyaṃ vidyādikaṃ yathā puṃsi kartari sā kartrī prayojakatayā yataḥ

plain_english: Thus when two imperceptible interiors occur for the two pumskala — of Maya-garbha-lord-power and the rest, interior knowledge interior.
sanskrit_cite: alakṣyāntarayoritthaṃ yadā puṃskalayorbhavet māyāgarbheśaśaktyāderantarajñānamāntaram

plain_english: Then Maya-purusha discrimination from all-karma destruction becomes — vijnanakala-state below Maya does not go; down goes the man.
sanskrit_cite: tadā māyāpuṃvivekaḥ sarvakarmakṣayādbhavet vijñānākalatā māyādhastānno yātyadhaḥ pumān

plain_english: In intellect-discrimination, when known, in pradhana-purusha interval — even so no karma-exhausted would be; in kala-covering that may arise.
sanskrit_cite: dhīpuṃviveke vijñāte pradhānapuruṣāntare api na kṣīṇakarmā syāt kalāyāṃ taddhi saṃbhavet

plain_english: Therefore by Samkhya view the established below pradhana would not transmigrate — in kala-purusha discrimination below Maya never goes.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ sāṃkhyadṛśā siddhaḥ pradhānādho na saṃsaret kalāpuṃsorviveke tu māyādho naiva gacchati

plain_english: Seeing the self separated from impurity, one would reach Shiva-hood — everywhere and lordly, power-descent here is co-cause.
sanskrit_cite: malādviviktamātmānaṃ paśyaṃstu śivatāṃ vrajet sarvatra caiśvaraḥ śaktipāto@tra sahakāraṇam

plain_english: Maya-garbha authorities, in the last of the two pure — this kala, by effect-difference, is other indeed inferred.
sanskrit_cite: māyāgarbhādhikārīyo dvayorantye tu nirmalaḥ seyaṃ kalā kāryabhedādanyaiva hyanumīyate

plain_english: Otherwise the universe would be one — for action, thus other-denial; thus in Matanga-scripture and the rest, what is declared, that kala itself.
sanskrit_cite: anyathaikaṃ bhavedviśvaṃ kāryāyetyanyanihnavaḥ iti mataṅgaśāstrādau yā proktā sā kalā svayam

plain_english: Having excluded by some-form agency, thus broken — endowed with some-form, which agency, how then would it be?
sanskrit_cite: kiṃcidrūpatayākṣipya kartṛtvamiti bhaṅgitaḥ kiṃcidrūpaviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ tatkathaṃ bhavet

plain_english: Of the ignorant thus, then produces limited-knowing-natured knowledge — intellect he sees; that vidya, intellect-mirror-dwelling.
sanskrit_cite: ajñasyeti tataḥ sūte kiṃcijjñatvātmikāṃ vidam buddhiṃ paśyati sā vidyā buddhidarpaṇacāriṇaḥ

plain_english: The own self distinguishes pleasure and related cognitions, delusion and the rest, and the karma-net standing in effect and cause.
sanskrit_cite: sukhādīn pratyayān mohaprabhṛtīn kāryakāraṇe karmajālaṃ ca tatrasthaṃ vivinakti nijātmanā

plain_english: But how can an intellect mixed with qualities, by discrimination, show pleasure, pain, or a delusion-natured object?
sanskrit_cite: buddhistu guṇasaṃkīrṇā vivekena kathaṃ sukham duḥkhaṃ mohātmakaṃ vāpi viṣayaṃ darśayedapi

plain_english: How does a transferring state remove knowability in the clear intellect, when another instrument acts in the person as agent?
sanskrit_cite: svacchāyāṃ dhiyi saṃkrāmanbhāvaḥ saṃvedyatāṃ katham tayā vinaiti sāpyanyatkaraṇaṃ puṃsi kartari

plain_english: Indeed a state shines from both person-light and bright mirror-like intellect; not so, it is its reflection.
sanskrit_cite: nanu cobhayataḥ śubhrādarśadaśīyadhīgatāt puṃsprakāśādbhāti bhāvaḥ maivaṃ tatpratibimbanam

plain_english: For primary illumination is inert; person-light illuminates what is external, so what construction is made of intellect?
sanskrit_cite: jaḍameva hi mukhyo@tha puṃsprakāśo@sya bhāsanam bahiḥsthasyaiva tasyāstu buddheḥ kiṃkalpanā kṛtā

plain_english: This is the ground of nondifference, and difference is examined here; therefore the state gone into intellect is within the range of the knowledge instrument.
sanskrit_cite: abhedabhūmireṣā ca bhedaśceha vicāryate tasmādbuddhigato bhāvo vidyākaraṇagocaraḥ

plain_english: The reflection of states is knowable, and intellect-construction does something from that; therefore certainly there is another thing.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvānāṃ pratibimbaṃ ca vedyaṃ dhīkalpanā tataḥ kiṃcittu kurute tasmānnūnamastyaparaṃ tu tat

plain_english: The raga-principle is declared as that which colors there; it is not merely nonattachment, because attachment-operation is there too.
sanskrit_cite: rāgatattvamiti proktaṃ yattatraivoparañjakam na cāvairāgyamātraṃ tattatrāpyāsaktivṛttitaḥ

plain_english: Even in a detached, satisfied one, subtle raga is established; time, praise, and so on measure agency from that.
sanskrit_cite: viraktāvapi tṛptasya sūkṣmarāgavyavasthiteḥ kālastuṭyādibhiścaitat kartṛtvaṃ kalayatyataḥ

plain_english: Effect-limiting agency necessarily disturbs time; necessity bears connection in the distinct sphere of effects.
sanskrit_cite: kāryāvacchedi kartṛtvaṃ kālo@vaśyaṃ kaliṣyati niyatiryojanāṃ dhatte viśiṣṭe kāryamaṇḍale

plain_english: Knowledge, raga, necessity, and time are this fourfold; kala-effect fills the enjoyer-state with standing enjoyership.
sanskrit_cite: vidyā rāgo@tha niyatiḥ kālaścaitaccatuṣṭayam kalākāryaṃ bhoktṛbhāve tiṣṭhadbhoktṛtvapūritam

plain_english: Maya, kala, raga, vidya, time, and necessity are the six declared coverings; in that state the bound soul stands in consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: māyā kalā rāgavidye kālo niyatireva ca kañcukāni ṣaḍuktāni saṃvidastatsthitau paśuḥ

plain_english: Knowing indeed occurs in body-city and knowables; this is sixfold contraction, while the unknowable is the atom.
sanskrit_cite: dehapuryaṣṭakādyeṣu vedyeṣu kila vedanam etatṣaṭkasasaṃkocaṃ yadavedyamasāvaṇuḥ

plain_english: It is said in the Shiva-body treatise; this covering is again stated by another mode, concerning all-self-going purity.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ śivatanuśāstre tadidaṃ bhaṅgyantareṇa punaḥ āvaraṇaṃ sarvātmagamaśuddhiranyāpyananyarūpeva

plain_english: Because it is burnable by Shiva's fire-ray nets, that covering is other-form by not-this priority; since it colors by own self, it is not other.
sanskrit_cite: śivadahanakiraṇajālairdāhyatvāt sā yato@nyarūpaiva anidaṃpūrvatayā yadrañjayati nijātmanā tato@nanyā

plain_english: For the naturally impure atom and Isha-cave, a threefold covering is applied; smooth kala is like a second consciousness of the clear.
sanskrit_cite: sahajāśuddhimato@ṇorīśaguhābhyāṃ hi kañcukastrividhaḥ tasya dvitīyacitiriva svacchasya niyujyate kalā ślakṣṇā

plain_english: By this, the bound soul of the knower becomes capable of enjoyment; its knowledge arises from kala like a lamp within refuge.
sanskrit_cite: anayā vidvasya paśorupabhogasamarthatā bhavati vidyā cāsya kalātaḥ śaraṇāntardīpakaprabhevābhūt

plain_english: It distinguishes pleasure-pain cognition for the bound soul; raga arises from the kala-principle like dye on pure cloth.
sanskrit_cite: sukhaduḥkhasaṃvidaṃ yā vivinakti paśorvibhāgena rāgaśca kalātattvācchucivastrakaṣāyavat samutpannaḥ

plain_english: One does not desire to abandon it, because worldly pleasure-cognition-bliss is present; the ignorance-stained one is enabled by the force of the three-quality covering.
sanskrit_cite: tyaktuṃ vāñchati na yataḥ saṃsṛtisukhasaṃvidānandam evamavidyāmalinaḥsamarthitastriguṇakañcukabalena

plain_english: The helpless bound soul falls downward in the deep enjoyment-womb; by this impurity is described, while kala and so on are like husk around the atom's shell.
sanskrit_cite: gahanopabhogagarbhe paśuravaśamadhomukhaḥ patati etena malaḥ kathitaḥ kambukavadaṇoḥ kalādikaṃ tuṣavat

plain_english: Thus in the kala-named principle, in a distinct part marked by some agency, agency is discussed as preceded by enjoyer.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kalākhyatattvasya kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇe viśeṣabhāge kartṛtvaṃ carcitaṃ bhoktṛpūrvakam

plain_english: As distinction, some part arises here as only-knowable, clear, and distinct; kala produces the primary.
sanskrit_cite: viśeṣaṇatayā yo@tra kiñcidbhāgastadotthitam vedyamātraṃ sphuṭaṃ bhinnaṃ pradhānaṃ sūyate kalā

plain_english: For kala equally produces the enjoyable and the enjoyer, not separated by difference-intention, mutually.
sanskrit_cite: samameva hi bhogyaṃ ca bhoktāraṃ ca prasūyate kalā bhedābhisaṃdhānādaviyuktaṃ parasparam

plain_english: Enjoyer-enjoyed nature would not be from separation, nor mutually in the dissolved state; maya too would not be anything.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktṛbhogyātmatā na syādviyogācca parasparam vilīnāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ syānmāyāsyāpi na kiṃcana

plain_english: Indeed from glorious Raurava onward, the raga-vidya-natured pair produces — kala indeed simultaneously from that manifest, thus the doctrine.
sanskrit_cite: nanu śrīmadrauravādau rāgavidyātmakaṃ dvayam sūte kalā hi yugapattato@vyaktamiti sthitiḥ

plain_english: Said here: this order shines, true — thus indeed enough: being colored one knows all, and knowing all here one is colored.
sanskrit_cite: uktamatra vibhātyeṣa kramaḥ satyaṃ tathā hyalam rajyamāno veda sarva vidaṃścāpyatra rajyate

plain_english: Nevertheless reality-existence here by us determined — and in that no sequence at all; or if any, that too from inversion.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi vastusatteyamihāsmābhirnirūpitā tasyāṃ ca na kramaḥ ko@pi syādvā so@pi viparyayāt

plain_english: Therefore admit no disagreement about the scripture-stated rule — thus only the experienced, which from pleasure-pain-delusion.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādvipratipattiṃ no kuryācchāstrodite vidhau evaṃ saṃvedyamātraṃ yat sukhaduḥkhavimohataḥ

plain_english: What will become from that is said equal-natured with that from the start — pleasure is sattva from luminosity; light is called delight.
sanskrit_cite: bhotsyate yattataḥ proktaṃ tatsāmyātmakamāditaḥ sukhaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśatvāt prakāśo hlāda ucyate

plain_english: Suffering is rajas from activity-nature — activity indeed crosses that; delusion is darkness, a covering, from light-absence-yoga.
sanskrit_cite: duḥkhaṃ rajaḥ kriyātmatvād kriyā hi tadatatkramaḥ mohastamo varaṇakaḥ prakāśābhāvayogataḥ

plain_english: Those agitated gunas produce effects — of the unagitated no heterogeneous effect would have been before.
sanskrit_cite: ta ete kṣobhamāpannā guṇāḥ kārya pratanvate akṣubdhasya vijātīyaṃ na syāt kāryamadaḥ purā

plain_english: Thus it is said in this treatise: the gunas know another tattva — worlds separately here shown by guna-difference.
sanskrit_cite: uktameveti śāstre@smin guṇāṃstattvāntaraṃ viduḥ bhuvanaṃ pṛthagevātra darśitaṃ guṇabhedataḥ

plain_english: Lord-will-power-agitated fickle man, for enjoyership — the independent Lord greatly agitates nature.
sanskrit_cite: īśvarecchāvaśakṣubdhalolikaṃ puruṣaṃ prati bhoktṛtvāya svatantreśaḥ prakṛtiṃ kṣobhayed bhṛśam

plain_english: By that, what Samkhya says about the freed atom — why would she not produce, from purusha's modifiability — that is no obstacle here.
sanskrit_cite: tena yaccodyate sāṃkhyaṃ muktāṇuṃ prati kiṃ na sā sūte puṃso vikāritvāditi tannātra bādhakam

plain_english: From gunas the buddhi-principle, stainless all around — from that purusha-light, knowable here, attains reflection.
sanskrit_cite: guṇebhyo buddhitattvaṃ tat sarvato nirmalaṃ tataḥ puṃsprakāśaḥ sa vedyo@tra pratibimbatvamārchati

plain_english: Object-reflection in that sense-made outside — not by that gateway; in projection appearance and the rest, such.
sanskrit_cite: viṣayapratibimbaṃ ca tasyāmakṣakṛtaṃ bahiḥ ataddvāraṃ samutprekṣāpratibhādiṣu tādṛśī

plain_english: Function-cognition may be of intellect — and also support, fixed; of self-awareness-light that cognition — inert too, enough.
sanskrit_cite: vṛttirbodho bhavedbuddheḥ sā cāpyālambanaṃ dhruvam ātmasaṃvitprakāśasya bodho@sau tajjaḍo@pyalam

plain_english: Buddhi-ego-made, such-like, of reflected-male-made — in light, in stained knowable, that I-thought-selfhood.
sanskrit_cite: buddherahaṃkṛt tādṛkṣe pratibimbitapuṃskṛteḥ prakāśe vedyakaluṣe yadahaṃmananātmatā

plain_english: By that agitation-formed fivefold wind impelled — for life; otherwise death again.
sanskrit_cite: tayā pañcavidhaścaiṣa vāyuḥ saṃrambharūpayā prerito jīvanāya syādanyathā maraṇaṃ punaḥ

plain_english: Therefore indeed from pure-self-freedom-I-nature, this from uncreated — but the other, so said, from the word krti.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva viśuddhātmasvātantryāhaṃsvabhāvataḥ akṛtrimādidaṃ tvanyadityuktaṃ kṛtiśabdataḥ

plain_english: Thus this ego's instrument-aggregate is determined — threefold its nature-aggregate: sattvic rajasic tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: ityayaṃ karaṇaskandho@haṃkārasya nirūpitaḥ tridhāsya prakṛtiskandhaḥ sāttvarājasatāmasaḥ

plain_english: Clearly from sattva-predominant ego touching enjoyer-portion — mind buddhi senses sixfold born; but difference is stated.
sanskrit_cite: sattvapradhānāhaṃkārādbhoktraṃśasparśinaḥ sphuṭam manobuddhyakṣaṣaṭkaṃ tu jātaṃ bhedastu kathyate

plain_english: Mind, which is all-object, thereby here intended to be stated — all-subtle-element agency is ego's qualifier.
sanskrit_cite: mano yatsarvaviṣayaṃ tenātra pravivakṣitam sarvatanmātrakartṛtvaṃ viśeṣaṇamahaṃkṛteḥ

plain_english: Buddhi ego mind, they say, in awakening-quest is instrument — by outer gods not, nor even by inward-facing made.
sanskrit_cite: buddhyahaṃkṛnmanaḥ prāhurbodhasaṃrabhaṇaiṣaṇe karaṇaṃ bāhyadevairyannaivāpyantarmukhaiḥ kṛtam

plain_english: And breath is no inner instrument, from inertness — of impelling nature; as cause of effort-desire-cognition portions — certain.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇaśca nāntaḥkaraṇaṃ jaḍatvāt preraṇātmanaḥ prayatnecchāvibodhāṃśahetutvāditi niścitam

plain_english: Determination and egoism, imagination and the rest, are not one-formed action — therefore three-ness, fitting in inner action, clearly.
sanskrit_cite: avasāyo@bhimānaśca kalpanā ceti na kriyā ekarūpā tatastritvaṃ yuktamantaḥkṛtau sphuṭam

plain_english: And buddhi is not insentient — instrumentality is mind's, as with pradhana; the like-pradhana-insentient-buddhi doctrine is rejected.
sanskrit_cite: na ca buddhirasaṃvedyā karaṇatvānmano yathā pradhānavadasaṃvedyabuddhivādastadujjhitaḥ

plain_english: Distinguished by sound-tanmatra-causality, that ego-principle — in ear as sense-organ, up to nose where smell-ness is indicated.
sanskrit_cite: śabdatanmātrahetutvaviśiṣṭā yā tvahaṃkṛtiḥ sā śrotre karaṇaṃ yāvadghrāṇe gandhatvabhoditā

plain_english: Because of material nature, awareness in objects is limited to ordinary acts like hearing and seeing.
sanskrit_cite: bhautikatvamato@pyastu niyamādviṣayeṣvalam ahaṃ śṛṇomi paśyāmi jighrāmītyādisaṃvidi

plain_english: Ego-nature is clearly established, so instrumentality is fitting through union with agency.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃtānugamādāhaṃkārikatvaṃ sphuṭaṃ sthitam karaṇatvamato yuktaṃ kartraśaspṛktvayogataḥ

plain_english: An instrument differs from the agent because it is driven, and another instrument would lead to instability.
sanskrit_cite: karturvibhinnaṃ karaṇaṃ preryatvāt karaṇaṃ kutaḥ karaṇāntaravāñchāyāṃ bhavettatrānavasthitiḥ

plain_english: Therefore, by freedom, the agent divides his own body and makes his own part into an instrument.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt svātantryayogena kartā svaṃ bhedayan vapuḥ karmāśasparśinaṃ svāṃśaṃ karaṇīkurute svayam

plain_english: Through meditation on that part, he makes something completely distinct, like an axe.
sanskrit_cite: karaṇīkṛtatatsvāṃśatanmayībhāvanāvaśāt karaṇīkurute@tyantavyatiriktaṃ kuṭhāravat

plain_english: Therefore, before cognition, the common instrument of impure knowledge is called power in action.
sanskrit_cite: tenāśuddhaiva vidyāsya sāmānyaṃ karaṇaṃ purā jñaptau kṛtau tu sāmānyaṃ kalā karaṇamucyate

plain_english: But in Matanga and others, power's agenthood is declared, and knowledge deserves instrumentality.
sanskrit_cite: nanu śrīmanmataṅgādau kalāyāḥ kartṛtoditā tasyāṃ satyāṃ hi vidyādyāḥ karaṇatvārhatājuṣaḥ

plain_english: It is said that agenthood is the cause of instrumentality, because without it other instruments have no stability.
sanskrit_cite: ucyate kartṛtaivoktā karaṇatve prayojikā tayā vinā tu nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ sthitiryataḥ

plain_english: From the common instrument group, knowledge is made separate, because without it other instruments lack their own stability.
sanskrit_cite: ato@sāmānyakaraṇavargāt tatra pṛthak kṛtā vidyāṃ vinā hi nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ nijā sthitiḥ

plain_english: Without power there is no agenthood or knowership, so power and knowledge are known as the person's chief instruments.
sanskrit_cite: kalāṃ vinā na tasyāśca kartṛtve jñātṛtā yataḥ kalāvidye tataḥ puṃso mukhyaṃ tatkaraṇaṃ viduḥ

plain_english: Therefore, even when mind and action senses are lacking, form and motion do not shine for the blind or lame.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva vihīne@pi buddhikarmendriyaiḥ kvacit andhe paṅgau rūpagatiprakāśo na na bhāsate

plain_english: But by common instrument power, even the blind attains perception of common form.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃtu sāmānyakaraṇabalādvedye@pi tādṛśi rūpasāmānya evāndhaḥ pratipattiṃ prapadyate

plain_english: Then from ego, beyond the subtle elements, action organs such as speech and hands are born.
sanskrit_cite: tata eva tvahaṃkārāt tanmātrasparśino@dhikam karmendriyāṇi vākpāṇipāyūpasthāṅghri jajñire

plain_english: Actions like speaking and taking are ego actions; an action organ is that capable of action.
sanskrit_cite: vacmyādade tyajāmyāśu visṛjāmi vrajāmi ca iti yāhaṃkriyā kāryakṣamā karmendriyaṃ tu tat

plain_english: Even when the hand is cut, the action-organ nature remains; its chief seat is the five-fingered hand.
sanskrit_cite: tena cchinnakarasyāsti hastaḥ karmendriyātmakaḥ tasya pradhānādhiṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ pañcāṅguliḥ karaḥ

plain_english: Even when taking by mouth, the established instrument is the hand; without it, action would not arise.
